title: Building the Engine While Flying the Plane: Launching the Figma MCP Server — Jesse Lumarie, Figma
reason: Substantial production eval case study: grading criteria, fixture construction, manual-to-automated workflow and frequent LLM-judge runs.

title: Multimodal Collaborative Agents for Next-Gen Commerce — Nidhi Kaushik Vyas, Google DeepMind
reason: Sustained explicit evaluation methodology throughout the talk; publisher transcript recovered, then mobile YouTube extraction also confirmed date and full captions.

title: The Death of Developer Advocates — Stephanie Jarmak, Sourcegraph
reason: Benchmarks, controlled tool comparisons, trace analysis and prompt-distribution experiments form the central technical evidence.

title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind
reason: Extended discussion of video/image evaluation, human-preference artifacts, automatic-rater limits and workflow-grounded checks; not merely a launch panel.

title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents
reason: Leadership talk includes a sustained concrete eval-set/rubric/harness optimization workflow and model-comparison example.

title: The AI bugpocalypse is here. Now what?
reason: Full transcript reviewed. Secure-by-design policy, memory-safe rewrites and cyber-defense access dominate. BaxBench vulnerability rates are cited briefly to motivate controls, without sustained benchmark construction, grading, comparison design or evaluation workflow; passing empirical citation is insufficient.

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Separating the Task from the Model
reason: Evaluation is one of the three central task-specification pillars, with sustained discussion of qualitative-feedback evaluation and optimization.

title: Vertical Mobility: Inference from MVP to Trillion-Parameter Workloads — Sitanshu Gupta, CoreWeave
reason: Full transcript reviewed. CoreWeave serverless/dedicated consumption, KV-cache locality, heterogeneous scheduling and inference acceleration dominate. Artificial Analysis versus OpenRouter traffic is briefly contrasted to support performance claims, but there is no sustained evaluation methodology.

title: Large clusters for small models — Daniel Svonava, Superlinked
reason: Adjacent but substantive performance-evaluation content: saturation-knee methodology, tuned runtime comparisons and measurement-driven autoresearch loops; not an application-quality eval tutorial.

title: Operating Distributed Inference Systems at Scale — Nishant Gupta & Naman Ahuja, Meta
reason: Full transcript reviewed. Distributed inference orchestration, scheduling, admission control, cascading failures and telemetry dominate. Successful tasks per dollar is an operating KPI, not a developed agent-quality evaluation or benchmark-design workflow.

title: Two Bugs That Hid in Plain Sight: A vLLM Debugging Detective Story — Asaf Gardin & Yuval Belfer
reason: Full transcript reviewed: differential token-log-probability checks against a Transformers reference, deterministic stress reproduction and silent-state-corruption diagnostics are substantial adjacent inference-correctness evaluation. Already summarized in results-3.json; do not duplicate.

title: Weight Folding, CUDA Streams, and the Bug That Made My Model Speak Backwards — Filip Makraduli
reason: Full transcript reviewed. Adjacent correctness-testing case contrasts unit tests/perplexity with longer generations that reveal a CUDA-stream race; already retained and summarized in results-3.json. This resolution defers to that existing adjacent inclusion rather than adding a duplicate.

title: The Dark Arts of Skill Engineering — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable)
reason: Full transcript reviewed, including Q&A: cross-model/cross-harness evals, simulated interactive users, design judges, per-line ablations and human judge-error analysis are substantial. Already summarized in results-3.json; do not duplicate.

title: The Frontier AI Inference Cloud for Agents — Byung-Gon (Gon) Chun, FriendliAI
reason: Full transcript reviewed. FriendliAI prefix caching, cache management, routing and agent-aware inference optimization dominate. Same-task demonstrations and customer speed claims advertise the stack; no sustained evaluation design or quality-grading method.

title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle
reason: Full transcript reviewed. Oracle workshop teaches agent memory, storage, semantic context, retrieval and harness assembly. Interactive component demos and bounded retry discussion do not establish a substantive eval suite, benchmark, grader or evaluation methodology.

title: Routing LLM Inference in Production: From Engine Signals to Policy — Qianru Lao & Lu Zhang, OpenAI
reason: Full transcript reviewed. OpenAI inference load balancing moves from engine-feedback control to explicit globally optimized routing weights. Offline latency profiles and live health signals serve infrastructure policy, not model/agent output evaluation; routing architecture is the subject.

title: What's New in Inference Engineering — Philip Kiely, Baseten
reason: Full transcript reviewed. Baseten surveys quantization, KV compaction, speculative decoding and training for inference. Performance findings illustrate optimization techniques, but no sustained benchmark methodology, evaluation workflow or model-quality grading design is developed.
